subject: iid models with a reference group

messages.author: 673086e375eccf25
messages.subject: iid models with a reference group
parts:
Dear all,

I would like to use the iid model in a slightly different way, fixing a certain (reference) group to 0.
This is equivalent to treatment contrasts in the regular lm model in R, rather than the sum-to-zero contrasts provided by the iid model.

The idea is to get a shrinked estimator for different treatment effects in comparison with a control group.

Is this possible?

Best,
Andreas

messages.author: b453c29749de564d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] iid models with a reference group
parts:
On Mon, 2017-04-24 at 07:35 -0700, Andreas Recke wrote:
> Dear all,
>
> I would like to use the iid model in a slightly different way, fixing
> a certain (reference) group to 0.
> This is equivalent to treatment contrasts in the regular lm model in
> R, rather than the sum-to-zero contrasts provided by the iid model.
>
> The idea is to get a shrinked estimator for different treatment
> effects in comparison with a control group.
>

just define the iid model for group 2...m. for group 1 just set the
idx to NA.

like here, instead of g=1:m, use g=c(NA, 2:m), and then

f(g, model="iid")



it is not advisable however, since the implied prior is not
exchangable. to make it exchangable, you can impose the sum to zero
constraint instead

g=1:m
f(g, model="iid", constr=TRUE)


H

To add to Håvards answer: 

If you want the contrasts, e.g. "Group 2 vs Group 1", you can get this with the sum-to-zero model too!

You just have to compute that part of the posterior, either with lincombs, or with posterior samples.

Haakon
